notes: Discrimination is concentrated in eval-0 (full generation): 10/10 with skill vs 5/10 baseline. All five baseline failures are the same failure mode — prose instead of mechanism: no machine-readable layout/pinned SHA (actual HEAD recorded nowhere), legacy tree left fully writable, no stable-ID problem register, no file:line citations, no machine-readable ledger with a walking-skeleton first milestone. That machine-state layer is the skill's measured value-add.

Evals 1 and 2 pass 100% in BOTH configurations — their assertions don't currently differentiate. Eval-1 is partly by design: the input workspace is skill-shaped and steered the baseline to a correct patch (evidence the 'executor needs no skill' architecture works). But graders found undetected protocol violations in the baseline arm: hand-edits to 'GENERATED — never hand-edit' guide files and a comment added to a frozen contract (docs/contracts/ddl.sql). Proposed tightenings: assert docs/contracts/* byte-identical, and a zero-diff re-render check on the guide.

Eval-2's honesty assertions were satisfied by the baseline's improvised [S]/[H]/[A]/[U] evidence-tagging — genuinely, not superficially (grader verified citations resolve and found zero fabrication). The 'weights labeled as proxy' assertion passed vacuously (no prioritization artifact existed). To discriminate, add assertions on machine-readable evidence state and on executability of the verification story.

Verification depth is the biggest unscored difference: both with-skill heavy runs booted the legacy app and captured golden traces at the pin (34 and 42 traces, with self-tests and an injected-divergence catch), while eval-0 baseline shipped an unexecuted test suite and eval-2 baseline's parity numbers are self-reported with no committed run report. An assertion requiring committed execution evidence (e.g. a harness baseline report in the workspace) would capture this.

Cost: with-skill averages ~164k tokens / 25 min vs ~33k / 8.5 min baseline (~3-5x per eval pair). Most of the delta is the harness work above, not skill-reading overhead (eval-1 with-skill was only +12% tokens over its baseline).

Mechanical checker produced 3 false positives that grader adjudication corrected (coincidental FIXED/REPAIR word matches in baseline prose; a slug-'decided' regex hit on a ruling-brief recommendation; a 'fabrication' hit on a request for future p95 data). Keep grade_checks.py as an evidence-gatherer, never as the verdict.

Scope: eval-2 baseline substantially exceeded the brief by implementing the FastAPI rewrite + migration tooling; the with-skill run honored the skill's 'generate, never rewrite' boundary. No assertion currently scores scope adherence.
n=1 per configuration — the +17pt delta rests on single runs; treat as directional until reruns.
